status: B7 data set (15 November 2026): the air-to-air weapons, fits, doctrine and the chain's numbers for the 1985 air battle (docs/air_battle/07_AIR_TO_AIR.md 5.1). Draft: the values the sources give are cited; everything else is a game value, named in each entry's game_values.
source: docs/research/air_battle_2026-11/aam_weapons.md and air_combat.md (the cited values and source ids); checo_1967_a2a; airwar_ru; mis; parsch_dusrm
notes: Every missile, gun and fit carries the year it entered service, gated by TheatreDef::year. Soviet equipment has a second year, allies_year, for the Pact's allies and our side. The 1991 AMRAAM, the AIM-9X and ASRAAM have no guidance class here and are absent; the R-27 and the R-73 are present with their real years (the R-73 for allies from 1988) and carried by no 1985 fit. AIM-9P, Sky Flash, Magic 1 and Super 530F have no usable date or envelope and are absent: their slots wait for a source (docs/air_battle/07_AIR_TO_AIR.md 7).

aams.name: K-13 (R-3S, AA-2 Atoll)
aams.source: checo_1967_a2a pp. 19-20 (the US intelligence view of the K-13 in 1967: minimum 1,000 m, launch under 2 g, 10 g at sea level, no guidance within 30 deg of the sun); ru_wiki_aam (series production 1960); the other values are game values
aams.notes: The 1967 view is the adversary's. The seeker's degradation 30-50 deg from the sun and the ground clutter (clutter_below) follow the same page; their numbers are game values. The maximum range is not in the sources read.

aams.name: R-13M (K-13M, AA-2-2 Atoll)
aams.source: ru_wiki_aam (freon-cooled Inei-70 seeker and a new proximity fuze, adopted 3 January 1974: unverified, Wikipedia only, no footnote); the values are game values
aams.notes: Adoption date unverified (aam_weapons.md aam-wp-01): the year 1974 is used because the research says the round existed by 1985. Ranges and limits are SAM3D's estimates on the K-13's.

aams.name: R-60 (AA-8 Aphid)
aams.source: airwar_ru (R-60: adopted 18 December 1973; 7.2 km at about 12 km, about a third near the ground; minimum 250 m; launch at up to 7 g; target 8 g; 3 kg rod warhead, damage radius 2.5 m; calculated kill chance 0.5 for one missile); ru_wiki_aam (seeker designation 12 deg, rear hemisphere only); the other values are game values
aams.notes: The target load is 8 g in the text and 12 g in the table: 8 used (aam_weapons.md section 4). The design figure is a design figure, not a combat rate: it is the ceiling of the last link only.

aams.name: R-60M (AA-8 Aphid)
aams.source: ru_wiki_aam (cooled Komar-M seeker, designation +-17 deg, usable head-on in close combat, calculated kill chance 0.9 after Markovsky and Perov 2005, not read); airwar_ru (R-60, for the shared round); the other values are game values
aams.notes: Adoption 1977 or the early 1980s (unverified; aam_weapons.md aam-wp-02): 1980 is a SAM3D estimate, before 1985 either way. allies_year 1984 is a SAM3D estimate for the Pact allies and our side, low confidence. The head-on range is a game value for close combat.

aams.name: R-23R (AA-7 Apex, semi-active)
aams.source: ru_wiki_aam (serial production 1973; the first Soviet missile able to engage against the ground; rod warhead 23 kg); mis (R-24: the R-24R raised the R-23's 25 km head-on and 15 km rear to 32 and 20 km: implied); the other values are game values
aams.notes: A Soviet comparison rates it above the AIM-7B and R.530 and a little below the AIM-7F (airwar_ru, MiG-23M).

aams.name: R-23T (AA-7 Apex, infrared)
aams.source: ru_wiki_aam (serial production 1973; the seeker locks head-on on the kinetic heating of the leading edges); the values are game values
aams.notes: Ranges: the R-23's 25 km head-on and 15 km rear are for the radar round; the infrared round's are SAM3D estimates.

aams.name: R-24R (AA-7 Apex, semi-active)
aams.source: mis (R-24: adopted for the MiG-23ML and MiG-23P by a decree of 6 April 1981; 32 km head-on and 20 km rear in the text; minimum 0.5 km; 10 s of autonomous flight, fired about 30 per cent beyond the seeker's lock range; 35 kg rod warhead, lethal radius 10 m; Mach 3.5); the other values are game values
aams.notes: The table in the source gives 50 km; the US view in 1982 was 10 to 14 nm (npic_1982_apex): 32 km used as the kinematic maximum head-on at height (aam_weapons.md section 4). allies_year 1981 is a SAM3D estimate, low confidence: the export dates are not given (unverified).

aams.name: R-24T (AA-7 Apex, infrared)
aams.source: mis (R-24: adopted by the decree of 6 April 1981; the all-aspect nitrogen-cooled seeker; 35 km in the table; minimum 0.5 km; lethal radius 10 m); the other values are game values
aams.notes: The rear range is the table's 35 km (low confidence); the head-on range is a game value. allies_year 1981 as the R-24R's.

aams.name: R-73 (AA-11 Archer)
aams.source: airwar_ru (R-73: adopted 22 June 1984; 30 km head-on; minimum 0.3 km from the rear; targets to 12 g; designation 45 deg in the table, 60 deg in the text; first exports in 1988); the other values are game values
aams.notes: In Soviet units only in 1985 (with the MiG-29, whose entry into frontal units is not established); no aircraft of the Pact faction in a 1985 war carries it. 45 deg is the missile cued by the aircraft's sights; 60 deg needs a helmet sight, post-period. The rear maximum is a game value.

aams.name: R-27R (AA-10 Alamo, semi-active): a later war's
aams.source: airwar_ru (R-27: the family formally adopted in 1987-1990; the R-27R 80 km, launch at up to 5 g, designation 50 deg for the radar round); the other values are game values
aams.notes: After 1985: kept out of the 1985 war by its year (docs/air_battle/07_AIR_TO_AIR.md 2.6). The allied year is a SAM3D estimate.

aams.name: R-27T (AA-10 Alamo, infrared): a later war's
aams.source: airwar_ru (R-27: the family formally adopted in 1987-1990; the R-27T 70 km, launch at up to 5 g, designation 55 deg for the infrared round); the other values are game values
aams.notes: After 1985: kept out of the 1985 war by its year.

aams.name: AIM-9B Sidewinder
aams.source: parsch_dusrm (AIM-9B: non-manoeuvring targets only, 900 m to 4.8 km); navy_factfiles (in operational use 1956); checo_1967_a2a (1967 reference round); the other values are game values
aams.notes: The 1967 reference round of the calibration (the USAF's AIM-9B/E in 1967). reliability 0.725 is the middle of the 1972 figure for AIM-9E rounds after captive carriage (25-30 per cent guidance failures: checo_1978_linebacker p. 30) applied to 1967 rounds: a SAM3D assumption (docs/air_battle/07_AIR_TO_AIR.md 3.1).

aams.name: AIM-7E Sparrow
aams.source: parsch_dusrm (AIM-7E from 1963: head-on up to 35 km in ideal conditions, about 5.5 km from the stern; the 1,500 m minimum is Parsch's figure for the Vietnam-era AIM-7); checo_1969_a2a (the F-4's radar arc 60 deg either side of the nose); the other values are game values
aams.notes: The 1967 reference round of the calibration. The AIM-7E-2 'dogfight' Sparrow of 1969 could be launched from about 610 m (checo_1969_a2a); not a separate entry. reliability as the AIM-9B's. The beam against the ground (AFIT 1982, afit_1982_vid) is the chain's beam_notch.

aams.name: AIM-9J Sidewinder
aams.source: parsch_dusrm (AIM-9J: about 10,000 built from 1972, mostly rebuilt B/E, actuators that doubled the single-plane g capability); the other values are game values
aams.notes: Rear aspect only. Ranges and limits are SAM3D estimates: no launch zone for the J was found (aam_weapons.md aam-nato-02).

aams.name: AIM-9L Sidewinder
aams.source: parsch_dusrm (AIM-9L: production 1978; all-aspect, argon-cooled indium antimonide seeker, laser proximity fuze, 9.4 kg warhead; a table gives 18 km for later rounds, the column alignment ambiguous); the other values are game values
aams.notes: All-aspect. The rear maximum is Parsch's ambiguous 18 km (low confidence); the head-on range and the limits are game values.

aams.name: AIM-9M Sidewinder
aams.source: parsch_dusrm (AIM-9M: production 1982); navy_factfiles (deliveries from 1983; better flare rejection, background discrimination and a reduced-smoke motor); the other values are game values
aams.notes: The year is the deliveries' (1983); production began in 1982.

aams.name: AIM-7F Sparrow
aams.source: parsch_dusrm (AIM-7F: production 1975-81, dual-thrust motor, 39 kg warhead); dubrov_1983 (envelope 5-50 km in the Soviet reading); the other values are game values
aams.notes: The Soviet reading's 5 km lower figure is not used as the minimum range. Semi-active: the launcher illuminates to impact (cbo_1986_amraam).

aams.name: AIM-7M Sparrow
aams.source: parsch_dusrm (AIM-7M: first firing of a YAIM-7M in 1980, production 1982, inverse monopulse seeker for low altitude and jamming); the other values are game values
aams.notes: The monopulse seeker is the higher clutter_below and flare_rejection (here: chaff and jamming), game values.

guns.name: GSh-23L 23 mm twin-barrel gun
guns.source: ru_wiki_aam (adopted 1965, after development from 1959: Wikipedia only, unverified); airwar_ru (200 rounds on the MiG-23MLD; about 4 s of firing on the MiG-23M); checo_1967_a2a p. 18 (the US view of the older NR-23 of the same calibre: effective range 3,500 ft, 1,067 m)
guns.notes: Effective range: the NR-23's, rounded to 1,000 m. kill_per_s is a game value calibrated with the pass's chance (docs/air_battle/07_AIR_TO_AIR.md 3.3).

guns.name: M61A1 Vulcan 20 mm gun
guns.source: airwar_ru (MiG-23M: a Soviet comparison gives the F-4E's gun 6-7 s of firing); aces_1976 (the F-105's M61 in 1965-73)
guns.notes: Loads and rates of the M61 in 1985 aircraft were not found in a usable source (aam_weapons.md aam-nato-08): the 6.5 s of the F-4E is used for every M61 fit. The effective range is a game value; the year is the gun's service before the Vietnam war (aces_1976 records F-105 gun kills from 1965).

guns.name: Aden 30 mm gun
guns.source: usn_falklands_1983 (the Sea Harrier carried two Aden 30 mm guns in 1982); the figures are game values: no rate or load found
guns.notes: Carried by the neutral's gun-armed jets (austrian_af_wiki: guns only; the calibre is a SAM3D assumption, unverified).

guns.name: 12.7 mm machine guns
guns.source: game value: the rebels' defected light jet carries guns (the theatre's data, docs/air_battle/07_AIR_TO_AIR.md 2.5); no calibre or load found
guns.notes: A placeholder gun for the rebels' Galeb class.

guns.name: GSh-6-30 30 mm six-barrel gun (MiG-27)
guns.source: hushkit_2020_mig27 (an Indian Air Force MiG-27 pilot: 260 rounds, 'just over 3 seconds to expend' at 5000 rounds a minute)
guns.notes: The firing window is the pilot's 3 s. The effective range and the kill rate are game values; the year is the MiG-27's, a SAM3D estimate.

guns.name: GSh-6-23 23 mm six-barrel gun (Su-24)
guns.source: airwar_ru (Su-24 and Su-24M: a GSh-6-23 with 500 rounds, read 18 Nov 2026, the page's text partly garbled)
guns.notes: firing_s is derived from the 500 rounds at a rate of about 9000 a minute, a SAM3D assumption (the rate was not read).

guns.name: GSh-30-2 30 mm twin-barrel gun (Su-25)
guns.source: airwar_ru (Su-25: a GSh-30-2 with 250 rounds, read 18 Nov 2026)
guns.notes: firing_s is derived from the 250 rounds at about 3000 a minute, a SAM3D assumption (the rate was not read).

guns.name: Two NR-30 30 mm guns (Su-17M3)
guns.source: airwar_ru (Su-17M3: two 30 mm guns, 80 rounds a barrel; read 18 Nov 2026, the designation garbled in the page's text)
guns.notes: firing_s is derived from 80 rounds a barrel at about 850 a minute, a SAM3D assumption.

guns.name: Two Mauser BK-27 27 mm guns (Tornado IDS)
guns.source: sam3d assumption: the Tornado IDS's two 27 mm Mauser guns are public reference knowledge not read from a registered source (unverified)

guns.name: GAU-8/A 30 mm gun used against aircraft (A-10A)
guns.source: wiki_guns (GAU-8 Avenger, a pointer: the A-10's gun); its use against aircraft is a SAM3D assumption (unverified)
guns.notes: A ground-attack gun: offered only against helicopters and slow aircraft (fight.slow_target_mps). Game values.

fits.source: airwar_ru (MiG-21MF: up to four K-13M, K-13, R-60 or R-60M; GSh-23L); docs/research/air_battle_2026-11/aam_weapons.md aam-our-01
fits.notes: Our fighter regiments' MiG-21 (the order of battle's 'mig21'). Two of each at a time is a SAM3D load. The R-60M from 1984 follows its estimated allies_year. RP-21 and RP-22 are placeholders in sensors.json.

fits.source: airwar_ru (R-60: the MiG-21MF and MiG-21bis among its carriers); docs/research/air_battle_2026-11/aam_weapons.md aam-our-01
fits.notes: As the MF.

fits.source: mis (R-24: adopted for the MiG-23ML by the decree of 6 April 1981); airwar_ru (MiG-23ML; the MiG-23MLD's typical load of two R-24 and four R-60, taken for the ML)
fits.notes: The Soviet frontal aviation's MiG-23ML of the Pact's 1985 war and our 3rd Fighter Regiment's twelve. The R-24T or R-23 are alternatives, not modelled. SRO-2M IFF, Lazur-SML link. export_fit is the stripped client variant (Bekaa's lower bound). The Pact's own MiG-23ML (type mig23ml_wp, B8) takes this fit: Soviet frontal aviation, the R-24 from 1981.

fits.source: lambeth_1984 (the Syrian export MiG-23s and MiG-21s: no R-23 or High Lark radar, at best the R-60: the lower bound); cordesman_1982
fits.notes: A stripped client variant, the fit a client's MiG-23 carries when export_fit is used. Not an aircraft type.

fits.source: airwar_ru (MiG-23MLD: 66 built new in 1984-85; typical load two R-24R or R-24T and four R-60; 200 rounds; 60 x 50 mm LO-43 flares; Parol IFF and the Lazur link, the IFF unverified for the MLD)
fits.notes: The 'or two R-73' of the page belongs to later variants and is not offered (docs/air_battle/07_AIR_TO_AIR.md 2.6).

fits.source: airwar_ru (R-60: carried by the MiG-27); hushkit_2020_mig27 (the gun)
fits.notes: Self-defence: two R-60 and the six-barrel gun (B8 gave the strike types their guns).

fits.source: airwar_ru (R-60: carried by the Su-24 for self-defence); airwar_ru (Su-24M: up to two R-60 or R-60M; the GSh-6-23)
fits.notes: Self-defence: two R-60 and the six-barrel gun.

fits.source: airwar_ru (R-60: carried by the Su-25 for self-defence); airwar_ru (Su-25: the GSh-30-2, an R-3 or R-60 class missile)
fits.notes: Self-defence: two R-60 and the twin-barrel gun.

fits.source: airwar_ru (R-60: carried by the Su-17); airwar_ru (Su-17M3: two 30 mm guns, an R-60)
fits.notes: Self-defence: two R-60 and two guns.

fits.source: parsch_dusrm (AIM-7F, AIM-7M, AIM-9L, AIM-9M dates); anderegg_2001 pp. 33, 161 (rifle scopes, 'Eagle Eye'); lambeth_1984
fits.notes: Four of each is a SAM3D load. No AMRAAM: it is a later war's weapon (cbo_1986_amraam: 1989 planned, 1991 in service) and has no guidance class in the data. Mark XII IFF, subject to spoofing (cbo_1986_amraam); visual identification is the rule (doctrine).

fits.source: cbo_1986_amraam ('F-16s cannot carry Sparrows'); parsch_dusrm (AIM-9L, AIM-9M)
fits.notes: The F-16A carries no radar missile in 1985: it fights with the AIM-9 and its gun. Two rounds is a SAM3D load.

fits.source: parsch_dusrm (AIM-7F, AIM-9J); checo_1978_linebacker p. 31 (the standard 1972 load: two or four AIM-7E-2 and four AIM-9E/J); airwar_ru (MiG-23M: the F-4E's gun 6-7 s)
fits.notes: TISEO adds identification range (vid_aid_m; anderegg_2001). Whether USAFE's F-4Es had the AIM-9L by 1985 was not found.

fits.source: parsch_dusrm (AIM-9J); the gun's absence and the load are SAM3D estimates, unverified
fits.notes: A Wild Weasel: an AIM-9 for its own defence, no gun (unverified).

fits.source: austrian_af_wiki (a combat jet of the neutral's 1985 air force: guns only, tier problem); the gun is a SAM3D assumption

fits.source: sam3d assumption: two AIM-9L for self-defence and the two guns (parsch_dusrm for the AIM-9L's year; the Tornado's carriage not read in a registered source, unverified)

fits.source: sam3d assumption: no air-to-air fit (no source read gives the F-111F an AIM-9 or a gun in 1985)
fits.notes: Decided in B8: it carries nothing for air combat; its defence is speed and low level.

fits.source: sam3d assumption: the AIM-9 on the A-10 is not dated in a source read (unverified), so only its gun
fits.notes: Decided in B8: the gun against helicopters and slow aircraft only.

fits.source: docs/air_battle/07_AIR_TO_AIR.md 2.5 (whether a Mi-24 could carry the R-60 is unverified)
fits.notes: Decided in B8: nothing until a source dates the R-60 on it.

fits.source: sam3d assumption: no armed helicopter of the four factions carries an air-to-air weapon in 1985
fits.notes: Decided in B8: every other helicopter (Mi-8, AB 212, Alouette III) carries nothing for air combat.

fits.source: sam3d assumption: the support, jamming and reconnaissance types and the rebels' light aircraft carry no air-to-air weapon in 1985
fits.notes: Decided in B8 so every type has a fit: the EF-111A, RF-4C, E-3A, KC-135, RC-135, MiG-25RB, Yak-28PP, A-50, Il-20, the rebels' An-2 and UTVA 75 carry nothing for air combat. Their defence is distance, height, speed or their escorts. The IFF is left 'none' here: these are never shooters, and our side's identification of them goes by the faction's own IFF rules in perception.

doctrine.source: afit_1982_vid (visual identification before a radar missile in central Europe); anderegg_2001 pp. 59, 82-84, 160 (pairs line abreast about a mile apart; 'left, low, lead'); checo_1969_a2a (the shot order of F-4E units: Sparrow, Sidewinder, gun); lambeth_1984 (the Bekaa's beam attacks)

fight.source: game values for the live and the abstract fight (docs/air_battle/07_AIR_TO_AIR.md 5.3, 5.6); the period anchors each names in its notes
fight.notes: Live: think_s the mode and shot check (2 Hz, staggered by a fixed key); radar_scan_s a radar's look; radar_az_deg its scan either side of the nose; contact_hold_s how long a contact is kept unseen; vid_m the eye's identification of a fighter (aam_weapons.md section 8: about 5-6 km by day); friendly_clear_m no friendly aircraft this near a contact for a BVR shot on the E-3A's word; gci_vector_s a controller's vector; gci_update_s and gci_error_m his radar picture; control_lost_s without a vector this long a flight has lost its controller; joker_s and bingo_s seconds of fight after the commit (no period number: air_combat.md nato-16); break_g a defender's break; gun_cone_deg and gun_aspect_deg the gun's angle off and the target's aspect a gun pass needs; extend_s an extension; claim_on_miss the share of misses claimed as kills (lambeth_1985: two shots called for every one observed at TOPGUN in 1980); slow_target_mps a target slow enough for a ground-attack gun. Abstract (A0): a0_intercept the share of our fighter threat that reaches a package; a0_detect_* our ground control finding it by day, by night, in poor weather and when the package is low; a0_rounds the passes fought; a0_meet_* the chance one escort flight of that kind engages our pair first, a0_awacs_meet its factor under the E-3A (2.0 from roadmap B14: the warned package's exchange against Teaball's 3.8:1 of August-October 1972, checo_1978_linebacker, in air_war_bench; a0_awacs_meet_mode0 the 1.5 before it, for a save made before B14); a0_surprise_* our first pass from the rear under GCI and with GCI jammed; a0_seen_* the enemy sees the attack in time (the E-3A's warning; the eye alone: red_baron_vol2, 13 of 16 MiG attacks on F-105 flights first seen with no warning); a0_gci_jammed our GCI's nets jammed when the package brings a jammer; a0_green_home green crews going home under jamming (reactions.md section 2.6: 30 per cent); a0_sarh_bvr_m, a0_sarh_vid_m, a0_ir_m and a0_gun_m the median ranges each weapon is fired from, with a0_range_sigma their lognormal spread.

ours.source: derived from data/command/oob_pannonia.json (the fighter division's three regiments, briefing decision 2) and docs/air_battle/08_OUR_FIGHTERS.md
ours.notes: Our fighter regiments as the abstract fight sees them until B10 makes them actors: each regiment's types and counts. A loss to our fighters is written with the regiment's id (LossRecord::by), so the debrief counts it apart.
